title: How to (Accidentally) Spot a Baku Founder. Tip #1
body: Ask where the company is registered. If he says ASAN Xidmət and the whole thing took forty minutes, correct, that's how it works and it's genuinely the best thing in the country. If he registered in Estonia or Georgia instead, the business is fine, the problem is getting paid, and he will explain the payment problem for eleven minutes without being asked. It's a sealed deal if he has three bank accounts in two countries and can tell you the transfer fee for each from memory.
caption:
Tip #1 😭 Baku sahibkarlar, this one is about you specifically.

title: How to (Accidentally) Spot a Baku Founder. Tip #2
body: Find out what the business actually is. Nine times out of ten it is one of four things: importing something from Turkey, importing something from China, a café, or a construction company that belongs to an uncle and is being described as his. Ask a second question. If the answer gets vaguer instead of clearer, it's the uncle's. It's a sealed deal if the office is his father's office and the sign on the door has a different surname.

title: How to (Accidentally) Spot a Baku Founder. Tip #3
body: Watch where he takes meetings. A real founder takes them at the office. A new one takes them at Chinar or Coffee Moffie and stays four hours on one americano. If he suggests meeting at Port Baku Mall on a weekday afternoon, the company has fewer than five people and one of them is his cousin. If he sends a location pin for a café in Yasamal, he's bootstrapping and he's serious. It's a sealed deal if the waiter knows his order and his business plan.

title: How to (Accidentally) Spot a Baku Founder. Tip #4
body: Ask about the startup certificate. The tax exemption is real, everyone wants it, and the ones who have it mention it the way other people mention a degree. Then ask about Innoland, the accelerators, the pitch events at the tech park. Everyone has pitched. Everyone has a deck. Nobody has closed the round. If he says he's "in talks with PASHA," that means one meeting happened in March. It's a sealed deal if the deck has been updated more times than the product.

Tip #4 😭 Baku sahibkarlar, this one is about you specifically.

title: How to (Accidentally) Spot a Baku Founder. Tip #5
body: Watch what happens with employees. He hired his cousin, then his cousin's friend, then someone from the region who is now the most competent person in the building. He pays late, apologises properly, and pays. Ask about the first employee who quit, because there is always a first one who quit, and the story is always told in a slightly wounded voice years later. It's a sealed deal if he still refers to the company as "biz" when there are two of them.

title: How to (Accidentally) Spot a Baku Founder. Tip #6
body: Ask what he sells on. If it's Instagram DMs, he's making money. If it's Tap.az, he's making more money and telling nobody. Wolt or Bolt Food means he's in food and the commission is destroying him and he will show you the number. Everyone is on Instagram, everyone complains about the reach, and everyone is quietly running ads they don't understand. It's a sealed deal if he's paying an SMM person more than he pays himself.

title: How to (Accidentally) Spot a Baku Founder. Tip #7
body: Ask about Dubai. Every Baku founder over a certain size has the Dubai conversation, the free zone, the visa, the flat in JVC, the friend who moved and posts about it. Half of them go. Half of them come back within two years and are much quieter about it afterward. Ask which category he's in and watch him decide in real time whether to be honest. It's a sealed deal if he already knows the name of a company formation agent in Dubai and has never met them.
